Hi Sam / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for the POC: 

Summary from the call
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference into Everwell search + triage pipeline (doctor notes + intake forms) for improved search relevance and a structured scheduling assistant.
- Key constraints: P95 latency target 280ms for user-facing suggestions, multi-region (US-EAST primary, EU fallback for EU patients), strict data residency for PHI in US-only environments.

Tech asks we need to unblock design (see items to send)
1) Volume profile: expected QPS during peak hour and typical doc length distribution (tokens).
2) Network: will calls originate from your VPC (private deployment) or public web tier?
3) Security: preferred auth pattern (mTLS vs token exchange), any proxy/bastion in front of services?

Our recommended initial approach (high level)
- SDK-based integration for the user-facing path (low-latency). We’ll provide an SDK bundle with example auth flows and structured-output examples for the scheduling tool calling.
- Model routing policy: latency-first for suggestions (primary low-latency variant), cost-aware fallback chain for batch/analytics jobs. Region routing: pin to us-east for US PHI, allow eu models only for EU-scoped traffic.
- Embeddings + reranker: embed candidate results and run a lightweight reranker (Redwood vector-store or your ES) for final ranking.

Next steps (proposed)
- Sam/Priya: share QPS and allowed egress topology by EOD Thu (19-Feb).
- Rishi + Laura: create a one-page ops playbook and SDK auth snippet; deliver by Wed (18-Feb).
- Schedule a 30m architecture sync for Thurs 19-Feb (I’ll propose times).

Attachments: draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.csv) for scope/timeline — please annotate.

Thanks — Kim

Kimberly Park

Kim — thanks for the recap, that matches our internal notes. Quick answers: 

1) Volume: Peak QPS ~220 (queries/sec) for search suggestions; typical doc length 150-600 tokens, doc corpus size ~3M records. Batch reranking jobs run nightly at ~150 QPS sustained for ~2 hours.
2) Network: calls will originate from our public web tier for the initial POC; long term we may route from a private VPC (depends on procurement).
3) Security: primary preference is token-based auth (short-lived tokens) for the web tier; security team is open to mTLS for service-to-service if needed.

A couple of asks from us:
- Can you outline a recommended routing policy that minimizes costs for nightly reranks but keeps interactive latency tight?
- We’ll need an initial SOC2 summary and where to send security questionnaires.

Priya will coordinate inputs and reply with logs/traffic examples. We can do Thurs 19-Feb at 11am PT for the sync.

— Sam
Sr. Product Manager, Everwell Health

Hi Sam / Priya — Rishi from Redwood infra/SE here. Thanks for the quick answers — below is a compact ops/architecture proposal that aligns with your latency/cost constraints and token-based auth preference. I attached a short SDK auth snippet (sdk-auth-snippet.txt) and a one-page set of QA answers as PDF (everwell-qa-answers.pdf).

Suggested architecture (POC)
- Path A (interactive, low latency):
  - Client (browser/mobile) -> your web tier -> Redwood SDK (hosted endpoint) via short-lived bearer tokens. We recommend token lifetime <= 60s for front-end requests and refresh via your auth server.
  - Routing policy: latency-first: primary route -> us-east low-latency model variant (quantized for CPU where applicable), fallback chain -> a slightly cheaper low-latency variant if primary constrained, final fallback -> small-context CPU variant for best-effort availability.
  - Batching: enable request batching at the SDK with max batch window 8–12ms to avoid pacing added latency; batch size target ~8–16 for your QPS profile.

- Path B (batch rerank/nightly):
  - Use Redwood Dedicated or bulk endpoint with cost-first routing. Pin to cheaper GPU/quantized path; schedule jobs during off-peak and use larger batch windows to reduce per-token cost.

Cross-cutting
- Region routing: we can configure tenant-aware routing rules so US PHI calls are forced to us-east (no cross-region egress). EU-origin traffic can route to eu-west model pool.
- Embeddings/reranking: pipeline we propose—generate embeddings for candidate docs via the embedding endpoint, run approximate nearest neighbor search (your ES or Redwood vector service), then call a lightweight reranker model (cost-optimized variant) to produce final scores.
- Structured output & tool calling: for the scheduling assistant, use structured JSON responses and the SDK’s tool-calling primitives to call your scheduler endpoint. Example pseudo-response schema in sdk-auth-snippet.txt.
- Auth patterns: we support short-lived JWTs, OAuth2 token exchange, and mutual TLS. For web-tier front-ends we recommend token exchange (front end gets ephemeral JWT from your auth server). If you move to VPC private deployment, we’ll implement mTLS between services.

Operational suggestions (SLOs/alerts)
- Set token expiry alarms and 5xx thresholds.
- Add a canary traffic route to test fallback behavior for model starvation.
- Trace tokens through Redwood Console for per-request latency breakdowns.

Open questions (need from Everwell)
- Can you share a sample token/refresh flow diagram?
- Confirm whether PHI will be present in the prompt text or only in metadata fields.

Attachments: everwell-qa-answers.pdf (QA page), sdk-auth-snippet.txt (examples).

Happy to walk through the SDK snippet in the Thursday sync.

Thanks — Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
